title: Welsh actor Matthew Rhys makes Emmy Awards history with double win
byline: Rhys was recognised at the prestigious US ceremony for his roles in supernatural TV comedy Widow’s Bay and psychological thriller The Beast In Me.

title: Severe lightning advisory issued for several areas
byline: The Department of Meteorology issued an advisory for severe lightning for North-central, North-western, Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Uva and Southern provinces and in Ampara, Batticaloa, Vavuniya and Mannar districts.

title: China tightens travel restrictions for citizens
byline: New rules governing travel to and from China have come into effect, a move that observers say will further tighten the government’s control over its citizens.

title: Govt. moves to introduce child-safety clearance for public service
byline: The Ministry of Women and Child Affairs has taken steps to introduce a mandatory clearance certificate for public-sector employees whose duties involve direct contact with children, Women and Child Affairs Minister Saroja Savithri Paulraj said.

title: US confirms for first time it has deployed space weapons
byline: The US has confirmed it deployed a space weapon in Earth’s orbit, the first time it has acknowledged such offensive capabilities.

title: Westminster’s time is coming to an end, Welsh, Scottish, Northern Irish leaders say
byline: The first ministers of Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have declared that ’’Westminster’s time is coming to an end’’.

title: Rumesh Tharanga returns home as javelins damaged during flight
byline: Sri Lankan javelin star Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage returned home early this morning following a historic victory at the World Ultimate Championships in Budapest, Hungary, where he claimed the gold medal in the men’s javelin throw with a stunning 91.09-metre effort.

title: Complaint to CID over alleged LTTE promotion at SLPP rally
byline: A complaint has been lodged with the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) over the alleged promotion of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) at the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) rally held in Anuradhapura.

title: President to launch Rs. 7.1 Bn hospital development projects in four districts
byline: Foundation stones will be laid for four major hospital development projects worth a total of Rs. 7,148 million in Anuradhapura, Trincomalee, Mannar and Mullaittivu, under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake on September 16.

title: King Charles to host AI executives as threat fears mount
byline: Britain’s King Charles will host the leaders of major artificial intelligence companies this week to discuss whether a shared set of principles is ​needed to guide a technology that has sparked growing warnings about its threat ‌to humanity.

title: Oil price surge weighs on CSE as ASPI slips below 21,350
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange opened the week lower on 14 September 2026, as the sharp rise in global oil prices weighed on investor sentiment and triggered broad-based selling across the market.

title: Railway unions maintain Sept. 17-18 strike
byline: The Joint Railway Trade Unions have decided to proceed with their planned two-day token strike on September 17 and 18, as no acceptable decision has been reached regarding the removal of the General Manager of Railways.

title: Sri Lanka, Thailand sign landmark agreements to strengthen labour cooperation
byline: Sri Lanka and Thailand today signed two landmark agreements aimed at strengthening labour cooperation and creating structured employment opportunities for Sri Lankan workers in Thailand.

title: Heavy rains exceeding 100 mm forecast in several areas
byline: The Meteorology Department has forecast cloudy skies with showers or thundershowers at times in the Western, Central, Sabaragamuwa, Southern and Uva provinces, as well as in the Batticaloa and Ampara districts, due to a low-level atmospheric disturbance in the vicinity of Sri Lanka.

title: Education must empower future generation to lead social transformation: PM
byline: Prime Minister and Minister of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Dr. Harini Amarasuriya said the Government’s objective is to create a learning environment that nurtures future leaders capable of driving positive social transformation through greater investment in education.

title: Thailand to recruit 10,000 Sri Lankan workers: Vijitha Herath
byline: Sri Lanka and Thailand signed landmark agreements today in Bangkok on Labour Cooperation and the Employment of Sri Lankan Workers in Thailand, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath said.

title: Daya Nellampitiya passes away
byline: Veteran Sri Lankan songstress Daya Nellampitiya has passed away at the age of 91, her family members said.

title: Preparations underway to implement education reforms in 2027
byline: A parliamentary committee has revealed that preparations are well underway for the implementation of education reforms in 2027, with activity books, teacher guides and modules for Grades 2 and 6 already prepared and teacher training programmes currently in progress.

title: New programme launched to qualify young people as “Construction Assistants”
byline: A new training programme has been launched to qualify young people as “Construction Assistants”, with the aim of providing them with dignified, secure and stable employment in the construction sector.

title: El Niño ‘100% certain’, Sri Lanka must strengthen disaster preparedness: Sajith
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has called for greater disaster preparedness, saying El Niño has become a “100% certainty” according to international climate organisations.

title: Certain individuals engaged in blackmailing MPs
byline: Certain Individuals are engaged in blackmailing Members of Parliament facing court cases in the guise of helping them to resolve such cases with the respective plaintiffs, MP Jagath Vithane alleged today.

title: Time to flush black money out of the system
byline: Start with a managed demonetization and withdrawal of the Rs. 5,000 note, make it harder to hoard illicit cash, conduct anonymous transactions and keep money beyond the reach of the formal economy. Bring hidden cash into the banking system, widen the tax net, curb bribery and illicit transactions and strike at Sri Lanka’s shadow economy.

title: Parliamentary seat falls vacant
byline: A vacancy has arisen in Parliament following the resignation of Sri Lanka Muslim Congress (SLMC) National List MP M.S. Abdul Wahid, the Election Commission has been informed.

title: CAA conducts over 1,000 raids on electrical, electronic goods
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has conducted more than 1,000 island-wide raids on electrical and electronic goods so far this year, including 204 raids carried out under a recent special programme.

title: Fuel price revision possible by end September: Energy Minister
byline: A fuel price revision could be introduced by the end of September, after taking into consideration the rise in global fuel prices and the prevailing situation in the Middle East, Energy Minister Anura Karunathilaka said today (14).

title: Two arrested over Dehiwala hand grenade attack
byline: Police have arrested two suspects in connection with a hand grenade attack on a residence along Sirisangabo Mawatha in Dehiwala, in which two brothers were killed.

title: Caroline Jurie, Chula Padmendra acquitted over Pushpika crown incident
byline: Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today ordered the acquittal of former Mrs. World Caroline Jurie and model Chula Padmendra in a case filed against them over an incident in which the crown worn by 2021 Mrs. Sri Lanka winner Pushpika de Silva was allegedly forcibly removed, causing injuries to her.

title: UK regularly raises accountability, disappearances with Sri Lanka- Foreign Office
byline: Britain has said it regularly raises issues of accountability, reconciliation and enforced disappearances with the Sri Lankan Government, while urging a credible and transparent investigation into the Chemmani mass graves that meets international standards.

title: Saudi pipeline outage threatens loss of 4% of global oil supply
byline: Saudi Arabia will run out of oil stocks for exports if it ‌doesn’t restart its major pipeline to the Red Sea within days, leading to a loss of up to 4% of global supply, Saudi oil buyers and traders said.

title: El Nino: Govt braces for any shortfall in essential food supplies
byline: In the event of fears that El Nino weather phenomenon will trigger a shortfall in imported essential supplies, the government has worked out an action plan to explore alternate markets , a Minister said.

title: Two rivers on flood alert
byline: The Irrigation Department has issued alerts for the Maguru Ganga and Attanagalu Oya as several parts of the country recorded heavy rainfall over the past 24 hours.

title: Sextortion: Don’t pay, don’t panic
byline: The Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (SLCERT) has urged the public to remain vigilant against sextortion, an online crime in which perpetrators threaten to share intimate images or videos unless victims meet their demands.

title: Subsidy, price caps or hike? Govt. weighs fuel options
byline: The government is considering several measures to address pressure on domestic fuel prices amid rising global crude oil costs, Power and Energy Minister Anura Karunathilaka has said.

title: “I respect the pain experienced by all communities affected by the conflict” – Gen. Shavendra Silva
byline: Even though 17 years have elapsed since the end of the armed conflict, many affected communities in the North, East and even in the South are still suffering. In an exclusive interview with the Daily Mirror, former Commander of the Army and Chief of Defence Staff General (Retd.) Shavendra Silva said that the pain and suffering endured by all communities deserve acknowledgement and dignity.

title: BRICS: While others lobbied,Sri Lanka lost ground
byline: As leaders of some of the world’s most influential emerging economies gathered in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Summit last weekend at Bharat Mandapam once again took centre stage in global diplomacy.

title: Government facing no threat: President
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said yesterday the government is not facing any threat and that the public rallies being held across the country are aimed at building a strong people’s movement to support the country’s development.

title: Two bags containing Rs. 320 Million ‘Kush’ found abandoned at BIA
byline: A stock of ‘Kush’ drugs valued at around Rs. 320 million was seized early this morning after being found abandoned near luggage belt No. 06 inside the Bandaranaike International Airport in Katunayake.

title: Landslide warnings issued for three districts
byline: The National Building Research Organisation (NBRO) has issued landslide early warnings for Colombo,Kalutara and Kegalle districts following adverse weather conditions prevailing in some parts of the country.

title: Heavy rain above 100mm possible in several provinces
byline: A low-level atmospheric disturbance persisting in the vicinity of Sri Lanka is expected to bring cloudy skies and showers or thundershowers to several parts of the country during the next 36 hours, the Meteorological Department said.

title: Cabinet clears $112M Port City waterfront project
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the designation of Prime Melwa (Private) Limited as a Primary Business of Strategic Importance, paving the way for tax exemptions and other incentives for its planned USD 112.2 million (approximately Rs. 15.9 billion) mixed-use development at Colombo Port City.

title: Government rejects claims of diaspora funding to NPP
byline: The Government today rejected allegations by MP Ramanathan Archchuna that the Tamil diaspora provided financial support to the National People’s Power (NPP) for its election campaign.

title: GMOA demands transport perks for specialist doctors due to public service debate
byline: The Government Medical Officers’ Association (GMOA) has called for transport facilities or a special transport allowance for specialist doctors serving in remote areas, arguing that failing to provide such benefits amounts to an injustice.

title: Court issues notice on National Hospital Director over failure to submit Suresh Sallay’s medical reports
byline: Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasekara today issued notice on the Director of the National Hospital, Colombo to appear before court on September 22 and show cause as to why the reports on the medical condition of Suresh Sallay, which were ordered by court on September 2, had not been submitted to court.

title: Rs. 2.5 bn additional funds for Paddy Marketing Board
byline: The Cabinet has approved the allocation of an additional Rs. 2.5 billion to the Paddy Marketing Board (PMB) to continue purchasing paddy harvested during the 2026 Yala season.

title: SITA Switzerland awarded SriLankan Airlines global network contract
byline: Cabinet approval has been granted to award the contract for providing global network infrastructure services to SriLankan Airlines Limited to SITA Switzerland SARL for a period of five years.

title: 39 new health projects planned for 2027
byline: The Government has approved 39 new development projects for 2027 aimed at improving public health services and addressing infrastructure deficiencies in hospitals and other government health institutions.

title: 2027 Appropriation Bill to be presented to Parliament
byline: Cabinet approval has been granted to publish the Appropriation Bill for the financial year 2027 in the Government Gazette and subsequently present it to Parliament for approval.

title: Sept. 25-Oct. 1 declared National Children’s Day Week
byline: The Cabinet has approved the declaration of September 25 to October 1, 2026 as ‘National Children’s Day Week - 2026’ to raise public awareness of children’s rights and strengthen community participation in child protection.

title: Free-roaming ponies raise accident concerns in Nuwara Eliya
byline: Residents of Nuwara Eliya have raised concerns over the risk of traffic accidents caused by ponies roaming freely on public roads while being used for tourism activities.

title: UNDP provides equipment to Government DNA laboratory
byline: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) has provided essential equipment to the DNA laboratory of the Government Analyst’s Department to enhance the country’s DNA testing capacity.

title: TID takes over probe into alleged LTTE promotion at SLPP Rally
byline: The complaint lodged with the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) over alleged promotion of the banned Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) at a Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) rally in Anuradhapura has been handed over to the Terrorism Investigation Division (TID) for investigation.

title: No ‘dog tax’ under new Rabies Act: Vet
byline: There is no new “dog tax” and no provision to jail people for feeding stray dogs under Sri Lanka’s newly gazetted Rabies Eradication and Dog Registration Act, Veterinary Surgeon and Animal Welfare Coalition (AWC) Executive Member Dr. Chamith Nanayakkara said.

title: Deep-sea fish weighing 300 Kg caught in Mannar waters
byline: A deep-sea fish weighing approximately 300 kilogrammes was caught in the waters off Mannar yesterday (14), attracting considerable attention among fishermen and the public.

title: Rumesh to get new Javelins after airport heartbreak
byline: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has moved swiftly to replace the competition javelins damaged during transit for Sri Lankan world champion Rumesh Tharanga, with the cost to be fully covered by the government.

title: Former Air Force Commander Donald Perera appears before FCID
byline: Former Commander of the Sri Lanka Air Force, Air Chief Marshal Donald Perera, appeared before the Financial Crimes Investigation Division (FCID) today to provide a statement in connection with investigations into the controversial MiG aircraft transaction.

title: ‘Sili-sili’ bags cannot be free
byline: Traders cannot provide “sili-sili” polythene bags free of charge to consumers when selling goods, the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) said.

title: Shani’s, Ravi’s Fundamental Rights violated by Easter attacks probe: SC
byline: The Supreme Court today declared that former IGP Deshabandu Tennakoon and two other police officers had violated the fundamental rights of retired Senior DIG and Secretary to the Ministry of Public Security Ravi Seneviratne and former CID Director Shani Abeysekara by initiating investigations against them in connection with the 2019 Easter Sunday attacks.

title: Ex-Transport Authority chairman arrested over Rs. 4.1 million loss
byline: The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) arrested the former Chairman of the Western Province Road Passenger Transport Authority, Opatha Vithanage Prasanna Sanjeewa, earlier today.

title: Heavy rainfall, thunderstorms expected in six provinces
byline: A low-level atmospheric disturbance persisting in the vicinity of Sri Lanka is expected to bring showers or thundershowers and heavy rainfall to several provinces, the Meteorological Department said today.

title: CSE extends decline as elevated oil prices keep sentiment cautious
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange closed lower for a second consecutive session on 15 September 2026, with both benchmark indices declining amid continued cautious investor sentiment and elevated global oil prices.

title: Kenya to host 2029 World Athletics Championships in African first
byline: Kenya will become the first African country to host the World Athletics Championships after winning the bid for the 2029 edition.

title: El Niño: Disaster drills ordered in landslide-prone districts
byline: Sri Lanka is stepping up disaster preparedness in several landslide-prone districts as authorities anticipate a shift towards wetter weather under the influence of El Niño over the coming months.

title: Suspected sabotage causes major Netherlands rail disruption
byline: Parts of the Netherlands, including Amsterdam, have been hit by major rail disruption after suspected sabotage to the tracks, the country’s railway infrastructure operator has said.

title: Sri Lanka urges citizens in Saudi Arabia to stay alert
byline: The Consulate General of Sri Lanka in Jeddah has issued an emergency advisory urging Sri Lankan citizens in the Western region of Saudi Arabia to remain alert amid the emerging situation in the region.

title: Online Police Clearance Certificate service suspended
byline: The online issuance of Police Clearance Certificates has been temporarily suspended due to system maintenance, the Sri Lanka Police said.

title: Dengue could rise again with upcoming rains
byline: Dengue breeding sites continue to be detected across the country through ongoing entomological surveys, Acting Director of the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU) Dr. Kapila Kannangara said.

title: Trump criticises Supreme Court after justices block mail-in ballot restrictions
byline: The US Supreme Court has rejected President Donald Trump’s plan to restrict voting by mail before November’s midterm elections, in a setback for the White House.
